p-image-ideogram 1.0.10 adds support for a new "very high" quality tier and updates configuration practices.

- Adds the premium path: use thinking: "very high" + image_size: "2K" for maximum quality or complex multi-text/panel scenes (costs ~2×; confirm with user before using).
- Documents five thinking levels ("very low", "low", "medium", "high", "very high") in place of four.
- Updates the agent guidance and parameter table for the new knob.
- Removes an obsolete skill-card.md file.

p-image-ideogram 1.0.9 changelog:

- Expanded README and guidance on when and how to use `p-image-ideogram` vs. related skills
- Added detailed agent habits and default parameter settings for various use cases (thinking, upsampling, image size)
- Included tables comparing `p-image-ideogram` with `p-image`, and when to use each skill
- Provided explicit instructions for typesetting, structured layout (JSON caption), and vertical profiles
- Added fidelity checks and prompt-crafting rules to ensure faithful and controlled outputs

- Bumped version to 1.0.1 and updated metadata accordingly.
- Removed the skill-card.md file.
- No user-facing functionality or API changes; documentation and packaging update only.

- Initial release of p-image-ideogram skill for high-fidelity, photorealistic image generation using Pruna Ideogram via Replicate deployment.
- Optimized for editorial portraits, hero plates, poster typography, and high-quality text rendering—distinguished from p-image (fast draft stills).
- Supports adjustable quality modes (`very low` to `very high`) and resolutions up to 2K for detailed outputs and legible text.
- Provides clear guidance on when to use this skill versus related Pruna skills (e.g., p-image, p-image-edit, p-image-try-on).
- Includes usage examples for both Python and HTTP (curl), plus best practices for prompt design and output quality control.
